channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description: Washington continued to operate as a change-of-pace back for the Raiders. He only saw two fewer carries than Ashton Jeanty, but the latter earned eight targets and led the team with 90 receiving yards. Washington was not targeted. Without any receiving work to fall back on, Washington is stuck in the RB4 ranks headed into a Week 12 matchup with Cleveland.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description: Johnston’s day was mostly quiet, although he did technically earn an end zone target on the Chargers’ sixth drive. The coaching staff tried to involve his post-catch skill set via a trick-play toss, but he was stuffed at the line of scrimmage. Johnston will be a shaky FLEX option against the Patriots next week, even if Justin Herbert clears the NFL’s concussion protocol.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Trevor Lawrence completed 25-of-47 attempts for 300 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Jaguars’ Week 11 loss to the Giants, adding three rushes for seven yards.
Tre’ Harris caught 2-of-2 targets for 28 yards in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description: Harris snagged a 22-yard pass against busted coverage in this one, but that was not his most consequential play. On the Chargers’ third drive, Harris ran a go route inside the red zone and managed to get behind his coverage defender. Justin Herbert uncorked it, and Harris dove for it, but unfortunately, the pass bounced off his hands in the back of the end zone. Jets EDGE David Bailey committed a roughing the passer penalty on the play, which the Chargers accepted, erasing it from the box score. Harris is a boom-bust FLEX against the Patriots next week, pending Justin Herbert’s (concussion) availability.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Ashton Jeanty rushed 11 times for 79 yards in the Raiders’ Week 11 loss to the Broncos, adding five catches for 90 yards.
item.description: Jeanty broke his first carry of 20 or more yards on a 46-yard sprint into the red zone in the second quarter. The Raiders’ offensive line finally cleared a lane for the former No. 6 overall pick and he ran to daylight before being tracked down by a pair of Broncos defenders inside the five. Per Next Gen Stats, he hit 21.4 MPH on the run, which goes down as his highest top speed since being drafted. Jeanty was also productive through the air. His highlight of the day was a 68-yard receiving touchdown. He beat his man on a wheel route and Fernando Mendoza hit him in stride for a massive score. It was enough for Jeanty to lead the Raiders in receiving for the second straight week. Jeanty’s elite receiving role alone will keep him in the middle of the RB2 ranks for his Week 12 date with the Browns on Sunday Night Football.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Ladd McConkey caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in the Chargers’ Week 11 loss to the Jets.
item.description: McConkey mostly ran short-to-intermediate routes from the slot today. Although he dropped what might have been a first-down pickup on the first drive after halftime, he made the most of his other opportunities. McConkey scored an 11-yard touchdown via an out route early in the fourth quarter, faking an in-breaker that left his coverage defender in the dust. McConkey scored again with roughly two minutes left, shaking Jets LB DeMario Davis on a six-yard hitch-and-go before snagging Justin Herbert’s throw in the end zone. It was an encouraging performance for the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver. Unfortunately, the team announced post-game that Herbert has entered the NFL’s concussion protocol. If Herbert is active, McConkey will be back in the WR2 tier next week against the Patriots.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Braelon Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding one reception for nine yards.
item.description: Allen racked up 17 touches in the No. 2 role behind featured starter Breece Hall. The Jets leaned heavily on their backfield today, with Geno Smith playing through an ankle injury. The coaching staff repeatedly called Allen’s number on multiple drives, allowing their burly backup to wear out Chargers defenders. Allen sealed the game with a 15-yard run up the middle, barreling through contact along the way. Allen must be rostered in all fantasy football formats as an elite bench stash at worst. He warrants FLEX consideration next week against the Dolphins.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Breece Hall rushed 20 times for 86 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers, adding three receptions for 14 yards and one touchdown.
item.description: The Jets’ coaching staff designed a run-heavy game plan with Geno Smith (ankle) playing through an injury. Hall and Braelon Allen split 40 touches between the two of them. Although Allen should be expected to remain regularly involved, and even got a little work inside the Chargers’ 20-yard line, the Jets made sure Hall was in the game when they got near, or inside, the Chargers’ 10-yard line. Hall scored on 2nd-and-goal from the Chargers’ seven-yard line by running a route across the backfield, behind the line, before catching a pass in the flats and turning upfield for the score. Hall is an RB1 against the Dolphins in Week 12.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Fernando Mendoza completed 18-of-37 passes for 267 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the Raiders’ 38-24, Week 11 loss to the Broncos.
item.description: Mendoza got off to a dreadfully slow start. The Raiders’ first three drives amounted to 11 net yards and a trio of punts. Mendoza was already down 17 by the time he got the ball back for his fourth series. Mendoza then finally settled in and moved the ball well. His first career passing touchdown came on a well-thrown wheel route to Ashton Jeanty. He led his running back to space and Jeanty did the rest. Mendoza tossed two more scores in the second half, but his comeback bid came to a screeching halt with a fourth-quarter pick-six. Broncos corner Ja’Quan McMillan jumped the route and rather easily took the interception to the house. Things get much easier for Mendoza in Week 12 when he takes on the Browns next week. He will be near the back of the QB2 mix for his third start.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Mason Taylor caught 2-of-2 targets for 25 yards in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Chargers.
item.description: Taylor made a nice, leaping grab for 19 yards on the Jets’ third drive before chipping in with a six-yarder on the next drive. He is a reliable starter in real life, but tougher to trust in fantasy football. He is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Dolphins next week.-Nic Bodiford
